profile.org_note: Three homebuilding areas (East, Central, West; also the 10-K reporting segments), each under an Area President who oversees roughly 5 to 9 divisions run by Division Presidents (Charlotte is styled a "region" under Charlotte Regional President Andrew Bodary); Financial Services is a fourth segment under Tawn Kelley. Divisions source land through their own VP Land Acquisition / VP Land Development (who report to the Division President), and deals are approved centrally by the Investment Committee chaired by Erik Heuser, Chief Corporate Operations Officer, with board approval above a set threshold; since 2026-07-24 the company is a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary and is to absorb Clayton Properties Group, but no post-merger field org chart is public.
profile.summary: National builder (Scottsdale, AZ) in 12 states and about 20 markets, selling entry-level, move-up and Esplanade resort-lifestyle homes, plus Yardly build-to-rent. At Q1 2026 it owned or controlled 75,626 lots, 51% off balance sheet, against a stated target of at least 65% controlled; it spent about $2.2 billion on land in 2025 and uses land banking (including an existing Kennedy Lewis land-bank agreement and a $3 billion Kennedy Lewis Yardly facility), seller financing and JVs. Berkshire Hathaway bought it for about $8.5 billion enterprise value (closed 2026-07-24); combined with Clayton Properties it is roughly the fourth-largest US homebuilding operation (about 23,000 closings in 2025), so land and capital decisions now sit inside a Berkshire balance sheet.

gaps: Treasurer / head of capital markets: not publicly named. The CFO is the senior finance officer; the credit agreement (Dec 2025) and supplemental indentures (Jul 2026) are signed by the Chief Legal Officer, S. Todd Merrill, not a treasurer.

Corporate head of land acquisition or land development (below Erik Heuser): not publicly named. Land deals are approved by a senior investment committee chaired by Heuser; division VPs of Land Acquisition / Land Development prepare the packages (job postings for Greenville-Spartanburg SC, Feb 2026, and Sarasota FL, Apr 2026, both now closed).
Division-level land VPs: none confirmed by name in a 2025-2026 source. Bill Dalton (Houston) is a lead only.

Post-merger org chart: Berkshire has said Taylor Morrison will lead a unified site-built operation with Clayton Properties Group, but no combined leadership roster or Clayton-to-Taylor Morrison reporting lines have been published.
Post-merger board: the 8-K of 2026-07-24 names Palmer, Merrill, VanHyfte and Heuser as directors of the surviving corporation; the investor-site page still shows the pre-merger public-company board.
Reporting lines: none are published; all reporting lines in this file are inferred from titles.
Texas subsidiary officers (Comptroller 2025 records) carry no functional titles; their roles (land, finance, operations) are not public.
Email pattern: not published; the company site shows only media@taylormorrison.com.
Regional and division presidents are in the separate divisions file (taylor-morrison.divisions.json).
Search limits: earnings-call transcripts (Motley Fool, MarketBeat, AOL) and builderonline.com could not be opened, so call remarks on land banking are not cited here.

Who the three Area Presidents report to: not published. No COO or Chief Field Operations Officer has been listed since early 2023 and the 2026 proxy names only CEO, CFO and CLO as executive officers, so a direct line to CEO Sheryl Palmer is inferred.

Carolinas reporting line: Charlotte Regional President Andrew Bodary (June 2026 release) and the Raleigh division are in the East segment, but Steve Kempton's bio names only Florida and Atlanta; whether the Carolinas report to him, or directly to corporate, is not publicly disclosed.

Corporate head of land (Chief Land Officer / EVP or SVP Land): no such role is publicly named in 2025-2026 sources; Erik Heuser (Chief Corporate Operations Officer, ex-VP Land Investments) chairs the Investment Committee and is the corporate land decision-maker of record.

Corporate Treasurer: the role exists (2025 Scottsdale Treasury Manager posting says it supports the Corporate Treasurer on all financings including JVs) but the holder is not publicly named. A third-party contact aggregator (connectplex.ai) lists a James Catlett as VP of Finance, Investor Relations and Treasury; not confirmed by any company or filing source, possibly stale, so not added as a row.
Post-merger: whether Clayton Properties Group's builders will be slotted into the East/Central/West areas or run as a separate group is not publicly disclosed.
